topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, tumor progression model, and the conceptual framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and evasion of inhibitory pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta, drive sustained proliferation and overcome growth-inhibitory controls.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and differentiate, contrasting developmental arrest across leukemias with APC-driven dysplasia in intestinal crypts.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis through p53 and mitochondrial regulators
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how mutations in p53 and imbalances in Bcl-2 family proteins prevent cells from committing to programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and cellular stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address telomere dynamics, TERT activation mechanisms, and the p53-mediated senescence and stress-response pathways that normally enforce replicative limits.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the alterations in cancer cell metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that produce epigenetic-modifying oncometabolites.

topics.label: Angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the requirement for vascularization to sustain tumor growth and the balance of regulatory factors governing the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the multistep metastatic cascade, the mechanical and environmental determinants of distant colonization, and the clonal genomic signatures associated with metastatic disease.

topics.label: Conclusion and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session by referencing recent hallmark perspectives, restating key takeaways, and inviting questions before practical sessions.
